title: Rapid qualification: technical guide for sales & SEs (v1)
body:
Purpose:
- One-page / quick-deck for SDRs, AEs, and Sales Engineers to rapidly diagnose inference needs and recommend the right Redwood offering (Hosted / Dedicated / Private).
- Focus: 5-minute technical qualification, 2-minute demo script, and 1-minute escalation checklist.

Audience and when to use:
- Use in discovery calls after product fit is established and before pricing discussion.
- Primary users: SDR handoff, SE pre-demo triage, AE negotiation moments where architecture or compliance are blockers.

Core thesis (speaker note):
- Customers choose inference deployments based on three axes: throughput/latency needs, data residency/compliance, and cost predictability. We map short signals to recommended pathing and a concrete next step (POC, capacity quote, or private deployment briefing).

Slide 1 — Quick decision flow (30s script)
- Ask two quick questions: 1) Are you hitting >10K tokens/sec sustained or >5K concurrent users? 2) Is customer data regulated/PII that cannot leave VPC or requires HSM?
- If Q1 yes => Dedicated. If Q2 yes => Private. Else => Hosted.
- Note: If both yes -> Private with Dedicated capacity (escalate to Solutions Eng).

Slide 2 — Top 8 technical qualifiers (use exact phrasing)
- Production concurrency expectations (peak RPS + burst tolerance)
- Typical sequence length (avg and 95th percentile tokens)
- Latency SLOs (p95 target in ms) and tail sensitivity
- Model family preference (open LLM, quantized, custom fine-tune)
- Data residency & KMS/HSM needs (in-flight, at-rest)
- Audit & retention windows for logs/requests
- Integration pattern (sync API calls, streaming, embedding bulk joins)
- Budget/price sensitivity: cost per 1M tokens target

Slide 3 — Rapid red flags (callout bullets for AE/SE)
- Unclear concurrency but planning to scale quickly -> request architecture workshop.
- Wants full model control and on-prem from day 1 -> propose Private discovery; expect longer lead time and contract.
- Low-latency requirement <5ms p95 -> not achievable for large open LLMs on hosted; discuss model distillation/edge options and set expectations.
- Regulatory note: If PCI/PHI/FERPA + retention for logs, route to Security & Compliance and Solutions Eng immediately.

Slide 4 — Micro-battlecards: persona-first value blurb (one-liners to use in pitch)
- Product Manager: "Reduce inference cost while keeping latency predictable — Redwood Optimize helps us tune batching and quantization automatically."
- Platform/Infra Lead: "Get a single API with consistent routing across hosted/dedicated/private — we can standardize your teams on one runtime."
- Security/Compliance: "Private deploys support KMS integration and audit logs; we can do on-prem air-gapped installs for regulated workloads."

Slide 5 — Demo play (2-minute demo script for SEs)
- Show: Hosted API latency dashboard (Console) -> open request trace -> show token-level cost breakdown -> explain fallback routing.
- Quick demo for Dedicated: show throughput graph + autoscale burst policy + canary rollback.
- Closing ask: "Can we run a very short POC? 1k concurrent synthetic users for 24h to surface latency/cost numbers?"

Slide 6 — Pricing signals & how to ask about budget (phrases)
- Signal phrases: "unit economics", "per-token cost", "predictable monthly spend", "capex vs opex".
- If they say "we need predictable cost": push Dedicated reserves conversation.
- If they say "we want lowest cost per token": discuss quantization and Redwood Optimize recommendations; coordinate Solutions Eng for quant profile.

Slide 7 — Objection handlers (short scripts)
- "We can self-host and save money": "Self-hosting moves day-2 ops to you — Redwood gives the runtime + autoscale + fallbacks so you avoid building complex KV cache/batching logic."
- "Latency is our biggest issue": "Let's run a focused benchmark with your sequence mix — we can suggest model variants and batching to meet SLOs."
- "We can’t send PII to hosted API": "That's expected; let's route to Private or Dedicated with customer-managed networking and KMS options. I'll schedule a security call."

Slide 8 — Quick escalation checklist (what info to gather before looping SE/Solutions Eng)
- Export of 24h synthetic traffic or production traces (sample requests)
- Peak concurrency and average sequence length (95th percentile)
- Model version and any custom fine-tune artifacts
- Security requirements: encryption keys, retention, audit needs
- Business timeline (pilot vs GA), budget runway

Slide 9 — Typical POC scoping templates (copyable lines)
- Hosted POC: "10k queries, 24 hours, capture traces + cost report. Responsible: SE + PM. Success metric: p95 latency within X ms and token cost <$Y/1k"
- Dedicated POC: "Reserved capacity estimate for 3 months, autoscale test for 48h, SLA targets validated. Responsible: Infra + SE."

Slide 10 — Next steps & internal owner tags (hand-off language)
- If privacy/regulatory => tag: @SolutionsEng + @Security (attach compliance questionnaire).
- If high throughput => tag: @InfraEng + request Dedicated capacity quote.
- If cost-first but low compliance => start Redwood Optimize eval and schedule cost walkthrough.

Appendix — Notes to self / TODOs (work-in-progress)
- Add small decision tree graphic (UX) — ask design to mock this week (JIRA:GT-8123).
- Add one-pager for legal talking points on KMS/HSM (waiting on Security review).
- Fill in sample numbers for common verticals (SaaS search, AI-assistants, e-comm chat) with expected token volumes.
- Follow up: gather recent Dedicated vs Hosted benchmark links and paste into Confluence page.

Speaker reminders (informal):
- Keep demo low-friction; show ROI quickly (tokens saved via caching/batching).
- Use customer language — "predictable spend" and "SLA" resonate with mid-market/enterprise.
- When in doubt, escalate early — private deployments have longer lead times.

Open questions for review meeting:
- Do we want a separate micro-battlecard for "embeddings-heavy" workloads? (Samir to prototype)
- How prescriptive should the Hosted -> Dedicated threshold be? current heuristic: >10k tokens/sec or >5k concurrent users.

References and links to paste into final deck:
- Console tracing docs (Confluence: link to tracing page)
- Benchmark repo (GH: repo/perf-benchmarks)
- Compliance checklist draft (CONFLUENCE:security-private-deploy-checklist)
